findings.problem: Mixed verb stems within paradigm
findings.reason: Infinitive and other forms use 'starte' (starter, ville starte, Startet), but preterite uses 'begyndte' from a different verb (begynde). Paradigm must stay on one stem.

findings.problem: Participle from different verb than rest of card
findings.reason: Present, preterite, and subjunctive use 'gemme sig' (hide), but the participle 'Bjærget' belongs to 'bjærge' (rescue). Participle should match the chosen paradigm: 'Gemt' or 'Skjult'.

findings.problem: Preterite from wrong verb stem
findings.reason: Card infinitive is 'Briste' (burst) with present 'Brister han', but preterite uses 'brød' from 'bryde' (break) in a phrasal idiom. Standard preterite of briste is 'bristede'.

findings.problem: Wrong past participle for infinitive stem
findings.reason: 'Brudt' is the participle of 'bryde' (break), not 'briste' (burst). For bersten the participle should be 'Bristet'.

findings.problem: Participle from different verb than rest of card
findings.reason: Infinitive through subjunctive consistently use 'love' (promise: Lover, Lovede, ville love), but participle 'Tilbudt' is from 'tilbyde' (offer). Should be 'Lovet' to match the paradigm.

findings.problem: Wrong verb meaning in infinitive
findings.reason: bitten means to beg/request, not to ask (spørge). The rest of the card correctly uses beg semantics (tigger, bad, ville bede, Bedt). Infinitive should align.

findings.problem: Infinitive does not match paradigm verb
findings.reason: All other forms use 'gælde' (Det gælder, Det gjaldt, Det ville gælde, Gældt). The infinitive phrase 'Komme til nytte' introduces a different construction and verb entirely.

findings.problem: Participle from different verb than rest of card
findings.reason: Infinitive through subjunctive use 'fange' (catch: fanger, fangede, ville fange), but participle 'Grebet' is from 'gribe' (grasp/seize), which better matches greifen. Participle should be 'Fanget' to match the paradigm.

findings.problem: Non-standard preterite form
findings.reason: Danish strong verb 'knibe' has preterite 'knib', not the regularised 'knibede'. Standard paradigm: kniber, knib, knibet.

findings.problem: Present tense from wrong verb stem
findings.reason: Infinitive is 'At stege' (roast/fry) but present uses 'bager' from 'bage' (bake). braten means to roast/fry, not bake.

findings.problem: Preterite from wrong verb stem
findings.reason: Uses 'bagte' (baked) instead of preterite of 'stege'. Should be 'stegte' to match infinitive 'At stege'.

findings.problem: Subjunctive uses wrong verb stem
findings.reason: Uses 'bage' (bake) instead of 'stege' (roast/fry), inconsistent with infinitive 'At stege' and participle 'Stegt'.

findings.problem: Wrong verb in subjunctive
findings.reason: 'bære' means to carry; bringen means to bring. Rest of card uses 'bringe' (bringer, bragte, Bragt). Subjunctive should use 'bringe', not 'bære'.

findings.problem: Present uses different verb than infinitive
findings.reason: Infinitive and participle use 'trænge ind' (penetrate), but present uses 'bryde ind' (break in). dringen means to penetrate/press through; forms should stay on one verb.

findings.problem: Preterite uses different verb than infinitive
findings.reason: Uses 'brød ind' (broke in) from 'bryde' instead of preterite of 'trænge ind'. Should be 'trængte ind' to match infinitive 'At trænge ind'.

findings.problem: Subjunctive uses different verb than infinitive
findings.reason: Uses 'bryde ind' instead of 'trænge ind', inconsistent with infinitive and participle on the same card.

findings.problem: Periphrastic phrase instead of infinitive
findings.reason: Infinitive slot requires a verb form. 'Det ser ud til' is an impersonal periphrasis, not an infinitive. Danish infinitive for dünken (to seem) should be 'At synes' or similar verb form.

findings.problem: Periphrastic phrase instead of conjugated present
findings.reason: Present-tense slot requires a conjugated verb. 'Det ser ud til' is a fixed impersonal phrase without finite verb inflection matching es dünkt.

findings.problem: Passive periphrasis instead of conjugated preterite
findings.reason: durfte requires the modal preterite 'måtte' (was allowed to). 'Var tilladt' is a passive adjective phrase, not a conjugated form of the modal verb matching the rest of the paradigm (må, Tilladt).

findings.problem: Passive periphrasis instead of subjunctive form
findings.reason: Konjunktiv II of dürfen should render as 'ville må' or 'måtte' depending on context, not the passive 'Var tilladt'. Should align with infinitive 'At få lov' and present 'Han må'.

findings.problem: Wrong verb meaning in present tense
findings.reason: empfehlen means to recommend; 'foreslår' means to suggest/propose. Infinitive correctly uses 'At anbefale' (recommend). Present should match.

findings.problem: Wrong verb meaning in preterite
findings.reason: 'Foreslog' (suggested) does not match empfahl (recommended). Should use preterite of 'anbefale' to stay consistent with infinitive and participle 'Anbefalet'.

findings.problem: Indicative future instead of subjunctive
findings.reason: Konjunktiv II requires 'ville' + infinitive, not indicative/future 'vil'. 'Han vil anbefale' is future tense, not subjunctive rendering of er empföhle.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within fliehen card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv and finite forms use løbe væk (run away) but the participle uses flygte (Flygtet). One German verb needs one Danish lemma across all forms.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within gedeihen card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv is At trives but present uses lykkes (succeed). Learners cannot reconcile two different lemmas for one German verb.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within gedeihen card.
findings.reason: Konjunktiv II uses lykkes while infinitiv is At trives; align to one stem across the card.

findings.problem: Preterite form in participle slot.
findings.reason: Trivedes is the preterite/passive of trives, not a past participle. gediehen (sein) requires Trivedet (har trivedet).

findings.problem: Past participle used instead of infinitive.
findings.reason: Malt is a participle; the infinitiv slot requires At male, matching maler/malede/Malt on this mahlen (grind) card.

findings.problem: Semantic mismatch vs German müssen (must).
findings.reason: Han har brug for means need; müssen is must/have to. Infinitiv At skulle on this card confirms skulle/må modal, not brug for.

findings.problem: Noun used instead of verb infinitive.
findings.reason: Ros is a noun (praise); infinitiv slot requires the verb At rose, matching roser/rost/rose/Roset on the same card.

findings.problem: Participle does not match raten/råde paradigm on card.
findings.reason: Other forms use råde (At råde, Han råder, Han rådede). Foreslået/nævnt (suggested/mentioned) breaks the lemma and is a slash variant chain.

findings.problem: Wrong smell direction for riechen.
findings.reason: Han lugter means he emits odor; riechen (er riecht) is perceiving smell. Danish needs kan lugte or an impersonal construction, not subject-emits-odor lugter.

findings.problem: Wrong verb in preterite slot.
findings.reason: Han brød sammen is bryde (break/collapse); ringen maps to kæmpe on infinitiv/praesens/participle (At kæmpe, Han kæmper, Kæmpet).

findings.problem: Wrong verb in Konjunktiv II slot.
findings.reason: Han ville bryde is bryde; ringen Konjunktiv must use kæmpe to match the rest of the card paradigm.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within rinnen card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv At sive and praesens Det siver use sive; preterite switches to flyde (Det flød).

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within rinnen card.
findings.reason: Konjunktiv II uses flyde while infinitiv/praesens use sive; one German verb needs one Danish lemma.

findings.problem: Third lemma on same rinnen card.
findings.reason: Størknet (coagulate) does not match sive/trickle forms; geronnen coagulate sense conflicts with At sive/Det siver on the same card.

findings.problem: Non-infinitive phrase in infinitiv slot.
findings.reason: Til salt is not a verb infinitive; salzen requires At salte, matching salter/saltede/Saltet on the same card.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schallen card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv uses gjalde (archaic/rare) but praesens, preterite, and participle all follow lyde (Det lyder / Det lød / Lydt). Learners see two different Danish lemmas for one German verb.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schinden card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv and Konjunktiv II use pine, but praesens, preterite, and participle use plage (Han plager / Han plagede / Plaget). schinden needs one consistent Danish lemma across all forms.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schinden card.
findings.reason: Konjunktiv II uses pine while all other indicative forms use plage. Align to plage (Han ville plage) or switch the whole card to pine.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schleifen card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv and present use slibe (grind/hone), but preterite uses kværne (mill/grind grain). schleifen in the sharpen/hone sense should stay on the slibe paradigm (Han sleb / Han slibede).

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schleifen card.
findings.reason: Participle uses polere (polish) while infinitiv is At slibe. Past participle of slibe is Slibet, not Poleret — three different Danish verbs appear on one card.

findings.problem: Semantic mismatch and paradigm split on schreien card.
findings.reason: schreien means scream/shriek; råbe means shout/call. Infinitiv (At skrige) and participle (Skreget) use skrige, but present uses råbe. Present should be Han skriger.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schreien card.
findings.reason: Preterite uses råbe (Råbte) while infinitiv and participle use skrige. Preterite of skrige is Han skreg.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schreien card.
findings.reason: Konjunktiv II uses råbe while the card lemma is skrige. Should be Han ville skrige.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schreiten card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv is At skride (stride) but present uses generic gå. schreiten denotes striding, not ordinary walking.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schreiten card.
findings.reason: Preterite uses gik (gå) while infinitiv and participle use skride (Skredet). Preterite of skride is Han skred.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schreiten card.
findings.reason: Konjunktiv II uses gå while the card lemma is skride.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schweigen card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv is At tie (be silent) but participle uses forstumme (become mute). Participle of tie is tiet.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within schwören card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv uses bande (curse/profanity) but all conjugated forms use sværge (swear an oath). schwören primarily maps to sværge in Danish.

findings.problem: Semantic mismatch on sinnen card.
findings.reason: sinnen means ponder/reflect (grunde over). undre sig means wonder/be surprised — a different verb and meaning. Konjunktiv II should follow grunde over (Han ville grunde over).

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within spleißen card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv is At splejse (splice, e.g. cables/fibers) but present uses generic forbinde (connect). spleißen in technical use maps to splejse throughout.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within springen card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv, present, Konjunktiv II, and participle use hoppe (Han hopper / Han ville hoppe / Hoppet), but preterite uses sprang from springe. Preterite of hoppe is Han hoppede.

findings.problem: Wrong part-of-speech for past participle.
findings.reason: Stående is a present participle/adjective ('standing'), not the past participle of stå. gestanden maps to Stået (havde stået).

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb stem within steigen card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv, present, and preterite use klatre (Han klatrer / Han klatrede), but participle uses Steget from stige. Participle of klatre is Klatret.

findings.problem: Inconsistent verb lemma within treffen card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv, Präsens, Präteritum, and Partizip II all use møde (møder / mødte / Mødt), but Konjunktiv II uses støde på (encounter). After owner repair aligned past to mødte, Konjunktiv II remains on a different verb.

findings.problem: Mixed verb stems within verderben card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv and Präsens use ødelægge/ødelægger (ruin/destroy), but Präteritum uses beskadigede from beskadige (damage). Learners cannot derive one Danish paradigm for verderben.

findings.problem: Mixed verb stems within verderben card.
findings.reason: Konjunktiv II uses skade (harm) while infinitiv is At ødelægge and Präsens is ødelægger. Conditional should mirror the same lemma as the rest of the card.

findings.problem: Participle from wrong verb stem.
findings.reason: Beskadiget is the participle of beskadige, not ødelægge. verdorben maps to ødelægge; standard participle is Ødelagt.

findings.problem: Added auf sense not present in German source.
findings.reason: er wuchs means he grew; voksede op specifically means grew up (aufwachsen). Präsens and other forms use plain vokse without op.

findings.problem: Participle field includes auxiliary verb.
findings.reason: All other cards store bare participles (Gjort, Blevet, Vokset). geworden → blevet; the auxiliary er is not used on other sein-auxiliary German verbs in this set (e.g. verb-165 Vokset, verb-168 Viget).

findings.problem: Present form uses different lemma than rest of card.
findings.reason: Infinitiv is At bebrejde and Präteritum/Konjunktiv use bebrejde/bebrejdede, but Präsens is an idiomatic phrase with giver (give). Learners cannot conjugate one verb across all forms.

findings.problem: Inverted word order in Konjunktiv II field.
findings.reason: Standard er-form cards use subject-first conditional (Han ville overveje). Präsens and Präteritum on this card were owner-repaired to Han overvejer / Han overvejede; Konjunktiv II still uses inverted Ville han overveje.
